deities: Goddess Kiriteshwari (Devi Vimala / Mukuteshwari, a form of Shakti)
festivals: Navaratri (flag: festival calendar not verified on official sources)

history.dynasty: Unknown; original temple pre-dates records; present temple rebuilt by Darpanarayan (Darponarayan), king of Lalgola / a Kanungo of Bengal
history.period: Ancient origins (tradition claims 1000+ years / Gupta era); original temple destroyed 1405 CE; present structure 19th century (sources conflict: 19th c. rebuild vs early-18th c. build by Darponarayan Bongadhikari; Sanskrit slab dated Saka 1736 = 1814 CE)
history.summary: One of the 51 Shakti Peethas (also called an Upa/Maha Peeth): the spot where the crown (kirit) — not a body part — of Goddess Sati fell; Peeth Devi is Vimala, Bhairava Sambarta. Claimed to be the oldest temple in Murshidabad district; a 16-temple complex with the old ruined south-facing shrine beside the present west-facing char-chala structure (noted by David McCutchion). No idol in the sanctum: a red stone / stone pedestal with a brass face of the goddess is worshipped. Legend says Nawab Mir Jafar sought the temple's charanamrita on his deathbed. FLAGS: (1) CSV 'state' column wrongly holds 'Murshidabad' — actual state is West Bengal; (2) CSV town 'Murshidabad' corrected to actual town Kiritkona village (near Lalbagh/Berhampore); (3) builder/period accounts conflict across sources (19th-c. rebuild per Wikipedia vs early-18th-c. construction per local guides; inscription Saka 1736 = 1814 CE).

name: Kiriteswari Temple
town_description: Kiritkona is a small village on the bank of the Bhagirathi River in the Lalbag subdivision of Murshidabad district, West Bengal, named after the goddess Kiriteshwari; it was noted on Rennell's maps and in the 18th-century Persian text Riyaz-us-Salatin as Tiruthkona.

travel.airport: Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose International Airport, Kolkata (flag: distance not verified)
travel.railway: Nearest railhead Berhampore; temple is ~19 km north of Berhampore by electric rickshaw / local transport (river crossing involved per visitor reviews)
travel.road: Road access via Berhampore (Lalbag); local e-rickshaws and vans from the town

visitor_information.best_time: October to March (winter); Durga Puja/Navaratri season
visitor_information.opening_hours: All day per visitor reviews (flag: official hours not verified; visitors report it opens very early in the morning, best by 8–8:30 AM)
